concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, had high-sensitive troponin T level of 0.309 ng/mL, and showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery, which are all indicative of acute coronary syndrome.
The patient had downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4 and an initial high-sensitive troponin T level of 0.309 ng/mL, which are consistent with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
The patient had ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, which are indicative of ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

The patient had thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery, contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion, and a significant drop in blood pressure to 60/40 mm Hg, which are all consistent with cardiogenic shock.
The ECG finding of R/S greater than 1 in leads V1-V2 and ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF suggests an inferior wall myocardial infarction.

rationales.F01: Sudden-onset chest pain is a common symptom of acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F05: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF is indicative of inferior wall myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin levels are a strong indicator of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery is a common cause of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F12: Hypotension is a sign of cardiogenic shock, which can occur in severe myocardial infarction.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's ECG findings of up to 2.0-mm ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, and new ST-segment elevation in V5-6, along with the elevated high-sensitive troponin T level, strongly support the diagnosis of ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction. The subsequent development of cardiogenic shock, as evidenced by the significant drop in blood pressure, is a complication of the myocardial infarction.
